messages:
alex: FYI customer on Dedicated reported a big throughput regression after last night's runtime tweak. They say sustained throughput dropped from ~110-130 rps to ~18-30 rps on their workload. P50 went 0.8s -> 1.8s, P95 ~1.6s -> 4.1s.

priya: Oof. Do we have request IDs / sample payloads? Also need region, model, quantization, and whether they used caching.

alex: Provided these request ids from the window: req_01H3Q9X0A1, req_01H3Q9Z2B4, req_01H3QAL7C8. Model: rwd-open/neo-2.7b-q4_0 (quantized), region: us-west2, pool: dedicated-8g. Client did a concurrency profile: 32 concurrent clients, each sending 1-stream generation, average prompt ~210 tokens, completion ~60 tokens. They attached a minimal prompt set.

alex: Paste of their curl reproducer (redacted API key):
```
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ME" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-open/neo-2.7b-q4_0","input":"<PROMPT>","max_tokens":60}'
```

priya: Good. Can you also capture the exact client behavior: connection reuse vs new TCP per request, HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2, and whether they used streaming? Those change batching characteristics.

alex: Customer says single persistent HTTP/1.1 connection per client (keep-alive), no streaming. They warm the cache briefly (they do a 3-request warmup) but most of their traffic is varying prompts so effective cache hit is low. SDK version: js-client 0.9.4.

jamie: I can try to reproduce. Two asks before I run: 1) provide the prompt set (can anonymize), 2) preferred concurrency run patterns (constant concurrency vs ramp), and 3) metric thresholds you want us to match.

alex: Prompt set (3 samples):
- "Summarize the following research abstract in two sentences." (~180 tokens)
- "Reformat the meeting notes into action items with owners." (~95 tokens)
- "Given the user message, produce a short empathetic reply and a suggested next step." (~220 tokens)

alex: Concurrency profile they used: 32 clients, each doing requests as fast as they get a response (approx steady-state), measured over a 10 minute window. They also ran one cold-cache run (server restart) and one warm-cache run (5-minute steady traffic before measurement).

priya: For repro bundle include:
- the raw request bodies (anonymized), 5 example request/response headers including x-request-id,
- client-side concurrency script or load generator config (k6, vegeta, or a simple node script),
- server logs for the corresponding request ids, and
- timeline of deploys around 2026-03-14 02:12Z.

alex: Uploaded initial artifacts and asked customer to approve us running internal load on their dedicated pool. support-bot: Debug bundle created: https://internal.artifacts.redwood/debug/1769804321-bundle.tar.gz

sre-bot: Automated note: debug bundle includes node load script (concurrency 32), raw payloads (3 prompts x 50 examples), and server logs trimmed to req_01H3Q9X0A1..req_01H3QAL7C8.

jamie: Good. Plan: I'll run two reproductions on Dedicated-8G in us-west2: (A) cold cache: restart target, run 2 minute ramp to 32 concurrent and measure 10-minute steady window; (B) warm cache: warm for 5 minutes at 32 concurrency then measure 10-minute window. I'll capture per-token throughput, per-request latency histograms, and GPU utilisation.

priya: Also add a test with smaller concurrency (8 and 16) to see nonlinear scaling points. And measure tail latency at high token counts (prompt+completion >250 tokens).

alex: Customer granted permission for internal repros. They also asked we check whether the recent kernel change to the attention kernel may have disabled an optimization for concurrency >16.

jamie: Noted. I'll include a run with the previous runtime build (sha: a1b2c3d) vs latest (sha: d4e5f6g) to compare.

jamie: ETA: repro runs + initial findings in ~3 hours. If I can reproduce, I'll produce a compact repro bundle (node script + prompt set + k6 config) that devs can run locally.

priya: Perfect. I'll add this to the latency regression board and tag runtime-eng for kernel attention check.

alex: Thanks — will keep customer updated. If anyone needs the raw debug link again: https://internal.artifacts.redwood/debug/1769804321-bundle.tar.gz :thumbsup:
